blocks.summary: The abstract defines low-quality reasoning in MLLMs and introduces SDR-MCoT with Selective Thinking and Step-wise Visual Enhancement.
The introduction motivates overthinking, insufficient visual use, and the need for a training-free self-driven multimodal CoT framework.
Related work covers multimodal large language models and multimodal chain-of-thought reasoning.
Selective Thinking computes the entropy of the first generated answer token and routes easy and difficult samples differently.
Step-wise Visual Enhancement computes relative attention, removes isolated attention sinks, selects high-attention patches, and amplifies their attention.
Experiments cover eight benchmarks, several MLLM backbones, and comparisons with No CoT, CoT, MMCoT, DDCoT, CCoT, and ICoT.
The conclusion restates that SDR-MCoT mitigates unnecessary reasoning and improves visual grounding without training.
Figure 1 shows that simple queries can be answered directly, while difficult queries benefit from visually enhanced step-by-step reasoning.
Figure 2 compares unnecessary CoT with the SDR-MCoT route on low- and high-difficulty examples.
Figure 3 gives the SDR-MCoT framework with entropy-based route selection and step-wise visual enhancement.
Figure 4 reports the negative relation between first-token entropy and M3CoT accuracy; no clean standalone crop was available.
Figure 5 visualizes option-aware attention, option-free attention, and relative attention for visual focus.
Table 1 compares main benchmark accuracy and generated-token consumption.
Table 2 ablates Selective Thinking and Visual Enhancement.
